Where Deals Are Lost

Where a Fintech Site Loses the Deal Before the Call

The ProblemStandard Agency

Legal pulls the page back after launch

Copy written without the regulated vocabulary in mind goes live, gets rewritten by compliance, and goes live again. The campaign window closes during the second pass, and the site ends up saying nothing at all.

The SOC 2 badge lands in the footer and stops

A prospect's risk function opens the site before the first call. If the badge sits in a footer with nothing around it, the reviewer cannot find what they were sent to check, and what they cannot find they assume is missing.

The site lags a quarter behind the roadmap

Fintech and AI companies move on funding rounds and product launches. When every change waits in a queue, the site describes the company as it was last quarter, and the investor who searches for you before the call sees the old one.

The SolutionThe Legency Approach

Launches hold their date through compliance review

Claims, disclosures and page copy are written for the review they will go through, so pages clear legal on the first pass and the campaign ships inside its window.

Trust signals sit where institutional buyers look

SOC 2, ISO 27001, data residency and subprocessors on a page that exists before anyone asks. The reviewer finds what they came for, and the site says "these people can handle our contract".

The site keeps pace with the roadmap

Requests go into a shared channel and come back live inside an agreed turnaround, so a pricing change is up before the sales call and the launch page is live the day the announcement goes out.

Original Fintech Research

The Fintech AI Visibility Index tracks how often fintech and AI brands are cited by AI assistants, so you know where you stand before a buyer asks one.

Compliance on the Page

Regulated Buyers Read Your Site Looking for Reasons to Stop

In fintech the website is part of the diligence. A prospect's risk function will open it before the first call, and what they cannot find they assume is missing. Our Webflow Enterprise agency selection checklist sets out the evidence to request before appointing a build partner.

Trust signals where they look

Certifications, data residency and subprocessors belong on a page that exists before anyone asks. Buried in a footer or held back for the sales deck, they do not help the person who was sent to check.

Claims that survive review

Regulated categories have language you cannot use and language you must. Copy written without that in mind gets rewritten by legal after launch, which is how sites end up saying nothing at all.

Page speed as a credibility signal

A slow, heavy site reads as an unserious one to a buyer whose own product is judged on latency. It is a soft signal that a buyer acts on.

Change control that exists

Knowing who changed what and when matters more here than in most sectors. A build with governance and a change record answers a question that will eventually be asked.

Why AI Visibility Matters Here First

Fintech Buyers Ask an Assistant Before They Ask a Vendor

Considered purchase, long research cycle, and a category where the buyer starts by asking what the options even are. That is the exact shape of question an AI assistant now answers with a shortlist.

What the Panel Measures

The shortlist forms early

  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Perplexity
  • Gemini

When the assistant names three companies and yours is missing, the buyer's shortlist is set without you, and no feature comparison gets you back onto it.

Being wrong is worse than being absent

Assistants describe companies from stale sources, so a fintech can be named for a product it retired or a market it left. Measuring what is said is the only way to find that.

Competitors are already there

In every panel we have run, a competitor is already being cited on the category questions. The question is who is in those answers today, and the panel names them.
